extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination staff and practitioners on handling, entry, refusal, and formatting of amendments to patent applications (including amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 and general amendment rules under 37 CFR 1.121). Covers procedural flow, form paragraphs, fees, and substantive limits (e.g., new matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks accompanying 37 CFR 1.312 amendments must state reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: As to amendments affecting the disclosure, the scope of any claim, or that add a claim, the remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state the reasons on which reliance is placed to show: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required for amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 that affect disclosure/claim scope or add claims. See MPEP § 713.04 and § 713.10 regarding interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 not intended for continued prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was never intended to provide a way for the continued prosecution of an application after it has been passed for issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommendation is against entry, a detailed statement of reasons is not necessary; a simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and brief reason usually suffice. Do not use 1.312 to continue prosecution after passage for issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient reasons for recommending non-entry of a 1.312 amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, any one of the following reasons is considered sufficient to recommend non-entry: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; or (C) the amendment would involve materially added work on the part of the Office (e.g., checking excessive editorial changes in the specification or claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are typical justifications for recommending non-entry under 37 CFR 1.312; where claims added are dependent claims usual reasons may be less likely though new matter, sufficiency, or undue multiplicity could arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after payment of the issue fee are not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendments should be filed after the date the issue fee has been paid. 37 CFR 1.312 no longer permits filing an amendment after the date the issue fee has been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph for PTOL-90 or PTO-90C to notify applicant; insert the date of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of copied patent claims after allowance not automatic; follow MPEP §2305.04
rubrics_metrics.description: See MPEP § 2305.04 for procedure when an amendment after notice of allowance includes one or more claims copied or substantially copied from a patent. The entry of the copied patent claims is not a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 714.19 and § 607 for additional fee requirements; copied claims may be refused entry under certain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed with motion under 37 CFR 1.633 not entered until motion granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment filed with a motion under 37 CFR 1.633(c)(2) applies to an application in issue, the amendment is not entered unless and until the motion has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter such amendments prior to grant of the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees required if amendment adds claims beyond paid number
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 adds claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for, additional fees are required. The amendment is not considered by the examiner unless accompanied by the full fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 607 and 35 U.S.C. 41; indicate fee payment or authorization to charge deposit/credit card as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing flow for 37 CFR 1.312 amendments affecting disclosure/claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 are sent by OIPE to the Publishing Division which forwards the proposed amendment, file, and drawing (if any) to the Technology Center (TC) which allowed the application. If filed directly with the TC, the paper should be forwarded to the Publishing Division to be flagged in PALM; then matched and returned to the TC for processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If class/subclass transferred after allowance, transmit proposed amendment to the new TC and notify Publishing Division. If the original allowing examiner is still employed but in a different TC, he/she may be consulted and given credit for time spent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner marking to indicate entry recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment is promptly considered by the examiner who indicates whether or not its entry is recommended by writing “Enter — 312,” “Do Not Enter” or “Enter In Part” thereon in red ink in the upper left corner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If favorably considered, it is entered and a Response to Rule 312 Communication (PTO-271) is prepared; the primary examiner stamps and signs PTO-271. Use form paragraph 7.85 or 7.86 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for entry/not entry/entered-in-part
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.85: 'Amendment Under 37 CFR 1.312 Entered' (useable for amendments not affecting claim scope by primary examiner or those affecting scope which require SPE signature). Form paragraph 7.87: 'Amendment Under 37 CFR 1.312 Not Entered' (specify reasons). Form paragraph 7.86: 'Amendment Under 37 CFR 1.312 Entered in Part'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommendation is completely adverse, type reasons for nonentry on PTO-271 signed by primary examiner. If entered-in-part, indicate which changes entered and which not, with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments embodying merely formal matters may be entered without SPE signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which embody merely the correction of formal matters in the specification, formal changes in a claim without changing the scope thereof, or the cancellation of claims may be indicated 'Enter Formal Matters Only' and do not require submission to the supervisory patent examiner prior to entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disapproved in whole or in part, they require the signature of the supervisory patent examiner. See MPEP § 714.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry-in-part rule and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The general rule that an amendment cannot be entered in part and refused in part should not be relaxed, but when an amendment contains plural changes some acceptable and some not, the acceptable changes should be entered. An indication of which changes have and have not been entered with appropriate explanation should follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry-in-part is not recommended unless the full additional fee, if any, accompanies the amendment. Handling similar to complete entry of 37 CFR 1.312 amendment; use form paragraph 7.86 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after period for reply (no petition/fee) are not formally entered
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is not prosecuted within the period set for reply and thereafter an amendment is filed without a petition for extension of time and fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a), such amendment shall be endorsed on the file wrapper but not formally entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff must immediately notify applicant by telephone and letter that amendment was not filed within time and application is abandoned unless a petition and fee are timely filed. See MPEP § 711.02 and § 710.02(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Technology Center Date vs Office Date stamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are stamped with the date of their receipt in the Technology Center ('Technology Center Date' stamp) and with an 'Office Date' stamp showing receipt by the Office. The Office Date should always be referred to in writing to the applicant regarding the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place Office Date stamp in left-hand corner and use Office Date in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt screening of mail for amendments replying to a final action
rubrics_metrics.description: All mail deliveries should be carefully screened to remove amendments replying to a final action in which a time period is running against the applicant. Such amendments should be processed within the next 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures uniform and prompt treatment, and allows supervisory patent examiner awareness for any special treatment (e.g., examiner on leave).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments presenting unpatentable claims or requiring new search ordinarily denied entry when prosecution closed
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments presenting an unpatentable claim, or a claim requiring a new search or otherwise raising a new issue in an application whose prosecution before the primary examiner has been closed are ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include cases where (1) all claims have been allowed, (2) all claims have been finally rejected (with exceptions), (3) some claims allowed and remainder finally rejected. See MPEP §§ 714.12–714.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.125 is denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.125 should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(q) and § 714.20 for further guidance; if parts of the paper are acceptable enterable portions and deny the substitute specification in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: A patent claim suggested by the examiner but not timely presented is denied entry (absent Commissioner authorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent claim suggested by the examiner and not presented within the time limit set or extension thereof will be denied entry unless entry is authorized by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2305.03 for related practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied patent claims may be refused entry under certain conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: While copied patent claims are generally admitted even though the application is under final rejection or on appeal, under certain conditions the claims may be refused entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2307.03 and § 2305.04 for conditions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned or improperly signed amendments are denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsigned or improperly signed amendment or one signed by a suspended or excluded attorney or agent will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signatures conform to rules; check for suspension/exclusion status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment filed after statutory period for reply expired is denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed in the Office after the expiration of the statutory period or set time period for reply and any extension thereof will ordinarily be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.17 for treatment and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments too imprecisely worded to permit accurate entry are denied
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment so worded that it cannot be entered with certain accuracy should be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.23 regarding defective directions and how to proceed if intent is unclear or location ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment canceling all claims with no substitute claim is denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the filing date canceling all of the claims and presenting no substitute claim or claims should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.01 for guidance; applicant should be notified as directed in MPEP §§ 714.03 and 714.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment in application no longer within examiner's jurisdiction denied except by Commissioner approval
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in an application no longer within the examiner’s jurisdiction will not be entered except in certain exceptions for applications in issue and only with approval of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.16 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to drawings held to contain new matter are not entered until new-matter issue resolved
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the drawing held by the examiner to contain new matter are not entered until the question of new matter is settled. This practice does not apply to amendments to the specification and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 608.04 and 706.03(o) for new matter procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendatory papers containing objectionable remarks in violation of 37 CFR 1.3 may be returned
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks that, in the opinion of the examiner, violates 37 CFR 1.3 will be submitted to the Technology Center Director for return to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.25 and § 1003. If TC Director determines violation, the paper will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not in permanent ink or on erasable paper are denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments not in permanent ink ('easily erasable paper') should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.07 for acceptable paper/ink standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments presenting claims beyond number previously paid and without fee denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper presenting claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for and not accompanied by the full fee for the claims or an authorization to charge the fee will be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 509 and § 714.16(c); require full fee or authorization to charge deposit account/credit card.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment cancelling elected invention and presenting only nonelected invention is nonresponsive and not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention should not be entered; it is nonresponsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be notified as directed in MPEP §§ 714.03 and 714.05; see MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (no replacement paragraphs/claims) are denied entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment including changes to the specification/claims which is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (i.e., one which does not include replacement paragraphs/claims) will be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.22 for the manner of making amendments and formatting requirements under 37 CFR 1.121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments that unduly interfere with preparation of first Office action may be denied
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment that unduly interferes with the preparation of a first Office action may be denied entry; factors are set forth in 37 CFR 1.115(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.03(a) for factors to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second/subsequent supplemental replies that unduly interfere with Office action preparation may be denied
rubrics_metrics.description: A second (or subsequent) supplemental reply that unduly interferes with an Office action being prepared in response to the previous reply may be denied entry; factors set forth in 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments that include unacceptable substitute specification should be entered in part
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting an unacceptable substitute specification along with other amendatory matter (e.g., claim changes) should be entered in part: deny entry of the substitute specification and enter the rest of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise applicant that substitute specification has not been entered. See 37 CFR 1.125 and MPEP § 608.01(q) for substitute specification submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: In applications where prosecution on the merits is closed (Ex Parte Quayle), amendments adding claims are entered only as to formal matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application where prosecution on the merits is closed, an amendment presented curing the noted formal defect and adding one or more claims some or all of which are not patentable or require further search will be entered only as to the formal matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has no right to have new claims considered or entered at this point in prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment accompanying motion granted only in part entered only to extent motion granted
rubrics_metrics.description: In an amendment accompanying a motion granted only in part, the amendment is entered only to the extent that the motion was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process entry consistent with the scope of the granted motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-March 1, 2001: amendments that rewrite specification but fail 1.121 should be entered in part
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after March 1, 2001 that amends the specification not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 and that presents rewritten or new claims should be entered in part: deny the proposal to amend the specification and enter the remainder that complies with 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise applicant that the specification amendments have not been entered; act on the application when reached in turn. See 37 CFR 1.121 and MPEP § 714.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent entry of amendment has no legal effect; mark 'Not Officially Entered'
rubrics_metrics.description: If technical support staff inadvertently enters an amendment when it should not have been entered, such entry is of no legal effect. Unless deleted, annotate the margin 'Not Officially Entered.' If to be retained in file, give paper number and list on file wrapper with notation 'Not Entered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.3 and MPEP § 714.25 for examples of papers which may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.121(a) overall requirement: amendments made by filing a compliant paper per §1.52
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in applications, other than reissue applications, are made by filing a paper, in compliance with § 1.52, directing that specified amendments be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the detailed subrules (b)-(j) of 37 CFR 1.121 for specific formatting and content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment by instruction to delete/replace/add paragraphs (37 CFR 1.121(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification (other than claims/listings) may be made by submitting: (i) an instruction unambiguously identifying the location to delete/replace/add paragraphs; (ii) any replacement/added paragraph(s) in clean form (no markings); and (iii) another version of replacement paragraph(s) on separate pages marked up to show all changes relative to the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up changes may be shown by brackets (deleted) or underlining (added) or equivalent; no marked-up version required for an added or deleted paragraph as long as the instruction states it has been added or deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment by replacement section (37 CFR 1.121(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If sections contain section headings, amendments may be made by referencing the section heading with an instruction to delete and replace that section, providing a replacement section in clean form, and a separate marked-up version showing all changes relative to previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up changes may be shown by brackets/underlining or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment by substitute specification (37 CFR 1.121(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification (other than claims) may be amended by submitting an instruction to replace the specification, a substitute specification in compliance with § 1.125(b), and another version of the substitute specification marked up to show all changes relative to the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §1.125(b) requirements for substitute specifications; include marked-up comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of deleted matter only by subsequent amendment presenting previously deleted matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Deleted matter may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously deleted matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to reinstate by mere notice; present the matter anew in compliance with amendment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amended by rewriting must be submitted in clean form with a marked-up version (37 CFR 1.121(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting the claim with all changes included. A rewritten or newly added claim must be in clean form (no markings) and accompanied by a parenthetical expression indicating status (e.g., 'amended','new'). If rewritten with same number, another version marked up to show all changes relative to previous version must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up version required for changed claims; parenthetical status must match between clean and marked-up versions. Marking may be brackets/underlining or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled claims reinstated only as new claims with new numbers (37 CFR 1.121(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim canceled by amendment (deleted in its entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reuse the same claim number to reinstate a canceled claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting a clean version of entire set of pending claims construed as cancellation of previous versions (37 CFR 1.121(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A clean version of the entire set of pending claims submitted in a single amendment paper is construed as directing cancellation of previous versions of any pending claims. A marked-up version is required only for claims being changed by the current amendment; any claim not accompanied by a marked-up version constitutes an assertion it was unchanged relative to the immediate prior version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should retain previous claim numbers when merely rewritten in clean form and submitted in proper numerical order; the examiner has no responsibility to ensure accuracy of claim rewriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings changes must be shown on separate paper in red and new compliant drawings filed upon approval (37 CFR 1.121(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the application drawings must be submitted on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval, new drawings in compliance with § 1.84 including the changes must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §1.84 for formal drawing requirements after examiner approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency: Office may require amendments to secure correspondence among claims/specification/drawings (37 CFR 1.121(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require applicant to amend to maintain consistency across disclosure elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter may be introduced by amendment (37 CFR 1.121(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition: additions that introduce new subject matter are not permitted; resolution may involve rejections or refusal to enter the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner's amendments (37 CFR 1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, including the claims, made by the Office in an examiner's amendment may be made by specific instructions to insert or delete subject matter set forth in the examiner's amendment; compliance with certain paragraphs of 1.121 is not required for examiner's amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow instructions identifying precise insertion/deletion points; paragraph (b)(1),(b)(2),(c)(1) compliance not required for examiner's amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reissue, reexamination, and provisional applications have special rules (37 CFR 1.121(h)-(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in reissue applications must be made in accordance with § 1.173. Proposed amendments in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530(d)-(j). Amendments to provisional applications are not normally made, but if made must comply with this section and will be placed in the provisional application file but may not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the cited sections for the special procedures and limitations applicable to these types of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-compliant amendments: Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment and advisory action procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary amendments and non-final amendments not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 are handled by technical support staff who notify applicant by mailing a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment. Amendments after final rejection are forwarded unentered to examiners who should address non-compliance in an advisory action. If amendment fails to place the application in condition for allowance, applicant will be notified in an advisory action. If time remains, applicant may re-submit or request an extension, but not beyond statutory deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners suggested to explain reasons for non-compliance in advisory actions; submission at or near statutory period should be accompanied by Notice of Appeal to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional consolidation of all pending claims into a single clean version (37 CFR 1.121(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit a clean version of all pending claims in one amendment paper to consolidate previous versions. When submitting rewritten claims in the clean set, parenthetical identifying status should not be rewritten; claims rewritten in clean form should retain the same claim number and be in proper numerical order. Submission of a clean set is construed as cancelling previous versions. A marked-up version only needed for claims being changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consolidation is beneficial for patent printing; the examiner has no responsibility to ensure the accuracy of applicant's claim rewriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective directions for entry of amendments: if correct place clear, proceed; if unclear, inform applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If directions are defective (e.g., inaccurate paragraph number or lack of precision), but correct place of entry is clear from context, the paper will be properly amended in the TC and examiner will initial the change and assume responsibility. Applicant should be informed of the alteration and entry in the next Office action. If doubt remains, indicate nonentry to applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.23 for examples and required notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of amendments: replacement paragraphs must be wholly rewritten and canceled matter reinstated only by subsequent amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a replacement paragraph/section to the specification is to be amended, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled so no interlineations or deletions appear in the clause as finally presented. Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. A claim canceled by amendment may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clean final text; follow rules for reinstatement (new insertion/new claim number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourtesy in papers: 37 CFR 1.3 requires conduct with decorum; objectionable papers may be returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys/agents are required to conduct business with the Office with decorum and courtesy. Papers presented in violation may be submitted to the Commissioner and returned. Technical support staff should briefly review papers before entry to determine whether discourteous remarks appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If remarks are discourteous, either ignore or submit paper to TC Director for possible return; complaints against examiners must be made in separate correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing back of reference under 37 CFR 1.131: substantive showing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected, the inventor (or qualified party) may submit an oath/declaration to establish invention prior to the effective date of the reference. Prior invention may not be established under this section in countries other than the U.S., NAFTA members, or WTO members (with date limitations). Prior invention may not be established if rejection is based on a U.S. patent/application publication of another claiming the same patentable invention or if based on a statutory bar. The showing must be of such character and weight to establish reduction to practice prior to the effective date, or conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence to reduction to practice or filing. Original exhibits or photocopies must accompany the affidavit/declaration or their absence satisfactorily explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the geographic and date limitations (no establishment outside designated countries or before specified dates in NAFTA/WTO members). See 37 CFR 1.131 for full requirements.
